snp4.11:1.1:
“From where have there arisen
quarrels, disputes,
snp4.11:1.4:
From where have they arisen?
Please tell me.”
snp4.11:2.1:
“From what is dear
there have arisen
quarrels, disputes,
snp4.11:2.4:
Tied up with stinginess
are quarrels & disputes.
snp4.11:2.5:
In the arising of disputes
is divisiveness.”
snp4.11:3.1:
“Where is the cause
of things dear in the world,
snp4.11:3.2: along with the greeds that go about in the world?
snp4.11:3.3:
And where is the cause
of the hopes & aims
snp4.11:3.4: for the sake of a person’s next life?”
snp4.11:4.1:
“Desires are the cause
of things dear in the world,
snp4.11:4.2: along with the greeds that go about in the world.
snp4.11:4.3:
And here too is the cause
of the hopes & aims
snp4.11:4.4: for the sake of a person’s next life.”
snp4.11:5.1:
“Now where is the cause
of desire in the world?
snp4.11:5.2:
And from where have there arisen
decisions,
snp4.11:5.4:
and all the qualities
described by the Contemplative?”
snp4.11:6.2:
In dependence on that,
desire arises.
snp4.11:6.3:
Having seen becoming & not-
with regard to forms,
snp4.11:6.4: a person gives rise to decisions in the world;
snp4.11:7.2:
these qualities, too,
when there exists
that very pair.
snp4.11:7.3:
A person perplexed
should train for the path of knowledge,
snp4.11:7.4:
for it’s in having known
that the Contemplative has spoken
of qualities/dhammas.”
snp4.11:8.1:
“Where is the cause
of appealing & un-?
snp4.11:8.2:
When what isn’t
do they not exist?
snp4.11:8.3:
And whatever is meant
by becoming & not- :
snp4.11:8.4:
Tell me,
Where is their cause?”
snp4.11:9.1:
“Contact is the cause
of appealing & un-.
snp4.11:9.2:
When contact isn’t,
they do not exist,
snp4.11:9.3:
along with what’s meant
by becoming & not- :
snp4.11:9.4:
I tell you,
from here is their cause.”
snp4.11:10.1:
“Now where is the cause
of contact in the world,
snp4.11:10.2:
and from where have graspings,
possessions, arisen?
snp4.11:10.3:
When what isn’t
does there not exist mine-ness?
snp4.11:10.4:
When what has disappeared
do contacts not touch?”
snp4.11:11.2:
In longing do graspings,
possessions have their cause.
snp4.11:11.3:
When longing isn’t,
mine-ness doesn’t exist.
snp4.11:11.4:
When forms have disappeared
contacts don’t touch.”
snp4.11:12.4:
My heart is set
on knowing how
they disappear.”
snp4.11:13.1:
“One not percipient of perceptions
not percipient of aberrant perceptions,
snp4.11:13.2:
not unpercipient,
nor percipient of what’s disappeared:
snp4.11:13.4:
for objectification-classifications
have their cause in perception.”
snp4.11:14.1:
“What we have asked,
you’ve expounded to us.
snp4.11:14.2:
We ask one thing more.
Please tell it.
snp4.11:14.3:
Do some of the wise
say that just this much is the utmost,
snp4.11:14.4: that purity of spirit is here?
snp4.11:14.5:
Or do they say
that it’s other than this?”
snp4.11:15.1:
“Some of the wise
say that just this much is the utmost,
snp4.11:15.2: that purity of spirit is here.
snp4.11:15.3:
But some of them,
who say they are skilled,
snp4.11:15.4:
say it’s the moment
with no clinging remaining.
snp4.11:16.1:
But knowing,
‘Having known, they still are dependent,’
snp4.11:16.3:
On knowing them, released,
he doesn’t get into disputes,
snp4.11:16.4:
doesn’t meet with becoming & not-
: He’s enlightened.”
